title: REDI-NET W-2 Water Processing
author: REDI-NET Consortium
materials: Discard the 30 µm filter membrane disc.
Select the program IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Flex_4wash on the instrument.
Select the program IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Duo_4wash on the instrument.

steps.title: Prepare PEG-8000 Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 40% PEG-8000 and 1.2 M NaCl solution.

substeps.instruction: Add a stir bar, 400 g PEG-8000, and 70 g NaCl into an empty 1L sterile autoclavable bottle.
Add sterile 1x PBS to a final volume of 1 L.
Autoclave the bottle with lid at 121 °C for 30 minutes.

Place the hot solution on a stirring hot plate and stir until it cools to room temperature. (Alternatively, if autoclave is unavailable, stir until crystals dissolve and filter through a 0.45 µm Corning Disposable Vacuum Filter/Storage System).
Store the solution at 4 °C.

steps.title: Set Up Filtration System
steps.instruction: Assemble the vacuum filtration apparatus to prevent contamination.

substeps.instruction: Wipe work surfaces with 70% ethanol.
Connect a 3 L Medi-Vac Canister to a vacuum pump via the vacuum outlet on the lid (ideally inside a biosafety cabinet).
Connect tubing to the air-in (patient) port on the lid and close unused inlets.
Turn on the pump to test vacuum suction via airflow.
Assemble the Magnetic Filter funnel, tubing, GL45 Screw Cap with 2-hose connector, and a 1 L dry glass bottle (autoclaved or bleach rinsed).
Position the Magnetic filter Funnel higher than the 1 L glass bottle.

steps.title: Initial Water Sample Pre-treatment
steps.instruction: Remove debris and turbidity from the raw water sample.

substeps.instruction: If the sample is very dirty, filter through sterile 8-ply gauze on a funnel using gravity to remove plants, mud, and microalgae (repeat if necessary).
If the sample has high turbidity, settle the water at 4 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Primary Filtration (30 µm, 10 µm, 5 µm)
steps.instruction: Perform sequential filtration of the water sample.

substeps.instruction: Wipe the magnetic funnel filter holder with 70% ethanol and air dry.
Place a 30 µm filter membrane disc on the holder and attach the top funnel cup.
Pour the settled water sample into the funnel, avoiding disturbing precipitation.
Turn on the pump (<15 psi) to collect filtrate in the bottle. Use a tube clip on the air outlet if flow rate control is needed to avoid splashing. Turn off the pump when the sample runs out.
Pour the filtrate into a sterile sampling bag (flat-wire closure) or clean bottle.
Repeat the filtration process using a 10 µm filter membrane, then a 5 µm filter membrane.
For each membrane (10 µm and 5 µm), store it in a sterile 60 mm Petri dish on ice, labeled with sample ID, date, and membrane size.

steps.title: PEG-8000 Treatment and Viral Capturing
steps.instruction: Concentrate viral particles using PEG-8000 followed by secondary filtration.

substeps.instruction: Add 187 mL of PEG-8000 solution to 750 mL of filtrate (or 62.5 mL solution to 250 mL filtrate) to achieve a final concentration of 8% PEG-8000. Mix well by shaking.
Store PEG-8000-added samples at 4 °C for at least 4 hours or overnight (do not exceed 24 hours).
Prepare positive control: 100 µL EBV and 50 µL DENV-1 standard in 180 mL sterile 1x PBS, then add 45 mL PEG-8000 solution.
Prepare negative control: 180 mL sterile 1x PBS, then add 45 mL PEG-8000 solution.
Re-assemble the filtration system and sequentially filter the treated sample through a 5 µm filter membrane, then a 0.45 µm filter membrane.
Store the 5 µm and 0.45 µm membranes in sterile 60 mm Petri dishes on ice, labeled with sample ID, date, and membrane size.

steps.title: Membrane Preservation and Preparation
steps.instruction: Preserve membranes and prepare them for lysis.

substeps.instruction: Evenly distribute 250 µL DNA/RNA Shield Reagent on the membranes in the Petri dishes, seal with parafilm, and store at -20 °C (short-term) or -80 °C (long-term).
Wipe forceps and surgical scissors with 70% ethanol.
Trim off the outer circle of the membrane where no water flowed through.
Cut the membranes into two halves.
Place 4 halves (one each of 10 µm, 5 µm pre-PEG, 5 µm post-PEG, and 0.45 µm post-PEG) in a new Petri dish; store unused halves at -20 °C.

steps.title: Sample Lysis and Beating
steps.instruction: Mechanically lyse the captured particles using a Bullet Blender.

substeps.instruction: Clean work surfaces with RNaseZap, then wipe with 70% molecular biology grade ethanol.
Prepare two Thermo Scientific Screw Cap 1.5 mL Micro Tubes per sample, each containing two spoons of 0.1 mm zirconium oxide beads and four 3.5 mm UFO beads.
Add 650 µL ATL-DX buffer (15 mL Buffer ATL + 100 µL Reagent DX) and 135 µL VXL buffer to each tube.
Cut the stacked membrane halves into pieces smaller than 1 mm x 3 mm and transfer them into the tubes (suggest Tube A for pre-PEG and Tube B for post-PEG membranes).
Add 20 µL Proteinase K (IndiMag kit) and incubate at 56 °C in a heat block shaker at 1400 rpm for 20 minutes (or vortex every 5 minutes if shaker is unavailable).
Pre-cool the Bullet Blender by adding dry ice to the cooling compartment and running the cooling program.
Load tubes into the Bullet Blender, set speed to 12 and time to 3, and start.
Let samples settle for 1 minute, then repeat the beating step.
Centrifuge the tubes at 12,000 x g, 4 °C, for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Nucleic Acid Extraction (KingFisher)
steps.instruction: Extract TNA using either the KingFisher Flex or Duo Prime instrument.

substeps.instruction: For KingFisher Flex: Load program 'IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Flex_4wash' and set up plates (Elution: 75 µL Nuclease-free water; Wash 4: 750 µL 100% ethanol; Wash 3: 750 µL 80% ethanol; Wash 2: 700 µL Buffer AW2; Wash 1: 700 µL Buffer AW1).

For KingFisher Duo Prime: Load program 'IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Duo_4wash' and set up Sample Plate (Row A: Lysate; Row B: 700 µL AW1; Row C: 700 µL AW2; Row D: 750 µL 80% ethanol; Row E: 750 µL 100% ethanol) and Elution Strip (Row A: 75 µL Nuclease-free water). Keep the door open during extraction to avoid ethanol vapor contamination.
Transfer 425 µL of supernatant from the lysed sample to the sample plate.
Add Buffer ACB and MagAttract Suspension G to each sample (Flex: 540 µL ACB + 20 µL MagAttract; Duo: 540 µL ACB + 25 µL MagAttract). Mix via inversion or Hula mixer for 2 minutes.
Run the instrument (~35 minutes).
Immediately remove the elution plate and pool elutes from the two bead tubes of the same sample into one final tube.

steps.title: Quantification and Storage
steps.instruction: Measure TNA concentration and store samples.

substeps.instruction: Use 3 µL of total nucleic acid for DNA and RNA measurement using a Qubit 4 Fluorometer with 1X dsDNA HS and RNA HS Assay Kits.
For DNA: Mix 3 µL sample with 197 µL 1x HS dsDNA Qubit Assay, vortex 5-10 seconds, and incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
For RNA: Prepare working solution (199 µL buffer + 1 µL dye), mix 3 µL sample with 197 µL working solution, vortex 5 seconds, and incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Store samples at -20 °C (< 2 weeks) or -80 °C for long-term storage, or proceed to testing.

steps.title: System Decontamination
steps.instruction: Clean the filtration system after use.

substeps.instruction: Rinse the magnetic funnel, water inlet tube, and 1 L glass bottle with 10% bleach, then rinse with deionized water.
Rinse the inlet tube and 1 L glass bottle with 70% ethanol, shake off residuals, and air dry.
Wipe the magnetic funnel with 70% ethanol.
